contract: X.Org twm 1.0.13.1 f.startwm behavior and wtwm safe Wayland handoff translation

manual.startwm-effect.text: This function kills \fItwm\fP and starts another window manager, as

command_execution.rule: F_STARTWM passes the decoded action string unchanged as the command operand of /bin/sh -c; shell parsing, expansion, redirection, pipelines, and command lookup are therefore shell behavior.

exec_failure.warning_argument: original Argv[0], not the attempted action string
exec_failure.rule: Because execlp returns only on failure, twm emits the warning, breaks from F_STARTWM, performs common input cleanup, and remains the active window manager.

required_checks: classify the configured action without executing it
resolve a registered in-process target or explicit cooperative adapter
verify target readiness and protocol-version compatibility
verify continuous ownership for every active display and client connection
verify native Wayland and Xwayland preservation independently

phases: prepare successor while wtwm retains every live session resource
obtain explicit readiness and preservation acknowledgement
commit ownership only after all protocol paths can remain live
retire the old handler only after the successor owns the complete session
ownership_boundaries: all native Wayland client connections, objects, and roles
Xwayland server and all X11 client connections
outputs, input devices, seats, and active grabs
managed geometry, mapping, iconification, and stacking
clipboard, primary selection, and window-manager selections
success_requires: a registered in-process successor or verified cooperative adapter
an acknowledged transfer plan for every ownership boundary
successor responsibility before wtwm relinquishes any resource

preserve: clipboard, primary selection, and window-manager selections

requirements.rule: The compatibility identity remains f.startwm STRING / F_STARTWM with the upstream /bin/sh -c command semantics and warn-and-continue exec failure path.
wtwm classifies and fully preflights the configured handoff before releasing or changing any current-session resource.
A generic shell command or target without a verified handoff adapter is reported as unsupported and is not executed while clients are active.
Unsupported, preflight-failed, readiness-failed, and pre-commit handoffs retain the compositor, native clients, Xwayland clients, focus, stacking, selections, and session ownership unchanged.
A successful handoff preserves live client connection identities and transfers every ownership boundary before wtwm retires the old handler.
The translation never claims that executing an arbitrary command can inherit or reconstruct wlroots/Wayland protocol state or take over generic client file descriptors.

verification_scenarios.oracle: The exact action string reaches /bin/sh -c and a successful execlp does not return to twm.
Failed execlp warns using original Argv[0], reaches common cleanup, and leaves twm running.
wtwm reports unsupported handoff without executing the shell command or changing any preserved session state.
The diagnostic identifies failed preflight and compositor, clients, focus, stacking, selections, and session ownership remain live and unchanged.
The registered handler assumes policy ownership atomically without process replacement, fd transfer, client disconnection, or loss of managed state.
The old handler retires only after the verified adapter acknowledges every ownership boundary and all existing connection identities remain live.
